question: A collection of non-empty subsets of the set $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ is called a simplex if, whenever a subset $S$ is included in the collection, any non-empty subset $T$ of $S$ is also included in the collection. Only one of the following collections of subsets of $\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$ is a simplex. Which one is it?

options.A: The collection of all subsets $S$ with the property that 1 belongs to $S$.
options.B: The collection of all subsets having exactly 4 elements.
options.C: The collection of all non-empty subsets which do not contain any even number.
options.D: The collection of all non-empty subsets except for the subset $\{1\}$.
